# Regex patterns that are safe to publish verbatim (they name shapes, not secrets).
# Format: <flags>\t<pattern>\t<why>   — flags is a JS RegExp flag string ("" or "i").
#
# ⛔ A pattern that spells out the thing it denies does not belong here — it publishes the leak in
# the file that exists to prevent it. Anything expressible as ONE token (a name, a domain's
# distinctive label, an issue-key prefix) goes into redaction-exact.txt as a hash instead, which
# catches it in every context. Only patterns whose distinctive part is a generic word or a shape
# survive below.
i	\bapp\.localhost\b	the source project's dev host convention
	C:\\Users\\	a machine-specific absolute path
	C:\\projects\\	a machine-specific absolute path
i	\w+\[bot\]	any review-bot handle — the SHAPE, so this file names no vendor (and the old name-based row could not match a bare handle: a trailing \b after "]" needs a word char after it)
i	\bpassword manager\b	discloses what the source product is
i	\bapps/(web|api|extension)/	a source-repo directory
i	\bpackages/ui/	a source-repo directory
i	\be2e/harness\b	a source-repo directory
i	\bmcp__[a-z_]+	an MCP tool identifier (adapters name tools on Call: lines only)
